answer: Each agent registers a cryptographic proof of stake that mints a unique crystal token tied to a hardware‑bound enclave, and the network records this token on an opal‑colored ledger. A quadratic bridge algorithm then aggregates reputation so that one verified identity contributes weight 1 while n sybil identities together contribute only √n, making the marginal gain of each fake node diminish rapidly. An attacker must acquire enough genuine hardware enclaves to earn linear weight, costing proportional resources rather than cheap account creation.
